2028 BMW iX7 Spotted With Production Split Headlights
15 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
The carparazzi have spotted a less camouflaged prototype of the BMW iX7, which is due in the fall of 2027 for the 2028 model year. As the brand's upcoming electric flagship, it should come as no surprise that designers went for distinctive styling that sets the iX7 apart from the iX5 and lesser electric sport utility vehicles.
Spied at the Nurburgring, the zero-emission prototype dons a new rear lighting signature, distinct from what you get from the iX5 and the outgoing internal combustion X7. Stacked horizontal elements on either side of the liftgate are on the menu, yet camouflage wrap still hides much of the finest of details.
Look a little closer, and you will see how each side has two slim LED bars stacked vertically. The circular reflectors, which sit much lower in the bumper, are not intended for production. There are no exhaust outlets to speak of, naturally, and the lack of an exhaust system allowed BMW designers to pen a very clean-looking bumper.
BMW decided on placing the rear wiper directly on the rear glass instead of concealing it beneath the roof spoiler, thus preserving the upright appearance of the internal combustion sibling. The X7 hails from the Spartanburg plant in the US, and Spartanburg will also serve as the stomping ground of the next-gen X7.
The side profile follows a similarly conservative approach, with the rear quarters remaining substantial. A relatively flat roof and tall-ish windows reinforce the impression of a cabin designed with three rows in mind. Multi-spoke wheels fill the arches, and the diameter of the brake rotors makes us wonder if this fellow is the dual-motor specification that slots below the M Performance bruiser.
Photo: SH Proshots Similar to earlier prototypes and mules, conventional door handles are nowhere to be seen. Instead, customers are presented with four winglet-style oddities that look just as weird as holding the pinky up while drinking a cuppa tea. Say what you will, but even Chinese safety boffins don't like this door handle design.
Very similar in styling to its inline-six and vee-eight brother, the iX7 sticks to the familiar split-headlight layout that includes slim daytime running lights in the upper corners and the main headlamp units in separate lower housings. Contrary to the Neue Klasse design language, the kidney grille spans a large section of the nose.
Although camouflage makes it hard to determine everything, that's a different grille design from what you get on the iX5. Based on an evolution of the Cluster Architecture, the iX7 should mirror the powertrain choices of the iX5 at the very least. In the case of the 60 xDrive, highlights include a 144-kWh battery in US specification, 800 volts for the electrical system, two drive units, and 570 horsepower.
Peak torque? According to BMW , said motors develop up to 593 pound-feet (805 Newton-meters). Charging power should be superlative on DC, just as expected from a CLAR-based luxury sport utility vehicle with many goodies lifted or adapted from Neue Klasse-based models. Reliable info suggests that production would kick off in September 2027, making the iX7 a 2028 model by US automotive standards.
The next X7 and iX7 are both codenamed G67, while their Alpina versions are referred to as G69. The introductory models are understood to be the iX7 60 xDrive, X7 40 xDrive, and the Alpina-branded X7 60 xDrive.
